tasks.notes: lib/db/prisma.ts exports a singleton PrismaClient wired to Prisma 7's mandatory driver adapter (`@prisma/adapter-pg`). Key choices: (1) adapter-pg over adapter-neon — Render runs a long-lived Node process against the Neon pooler URL, the HTTP serverless adapter is for edge/serverless cold-start runtimes we don't target. (2) `pg` is a transitive dep of `@prisma/adapter-pg@7.8.0` — no need to install it separately (verified in adapter's package.json). (3) `import 'server-only'` at the top so an accidental client-component import fails at build time. (4) Singleton uses `globalThis.__beatyourselfPrisma` cache, gated on `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` — in prod a fresh client per worker, in dev HMR reuses the cached instance to keep Neon's free-tier connection cap from being exhausted. (5) Variable name `__beatyourselfPrisma` (not generic `__prisma`) to avoid colliding with any other Prisma installs in node_modules. Verification (all pass): `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` (production build emits the prisma module without errors); functional smoke against Neon via a one-off node script (`new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg(DATABASE_URL) }).user.findMany()` → []; `.challenge.findMany()` → []); HMR singleton smoke: started `npm run dev` with env vars piped from .env.local, hit a temporary `/api/smoke-prisma` route 5 times across 3 HMR file-touches on lib/db/prisma.ts and the route itself — every response was `{userCount:0,challengeCount:0}` and the dev-server log shows zero Prisma instance warnings. tasks.notes: lib/crypto/cipher.ts exports encrypt/decrypt using node:crypto AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte IV (NIST SP 800-38D recommended length) and 16-byte auth tag. Wire format is `iv:authTag:ciphertext` with each segment base64. Key handling: cipher reads process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY at call time (not module-load time) so unit tests can stub the key without satisfying the full @/config/env zod schema; this also means the env validator's broader checks still apply when the Next.js runtime boots. Key accepts either 64-char hex or 44-char base64 (validated to land at 32 bytes after decode). `import 'server-only'` at top of cipher.ts blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. Test infra: installed vitest@4.1.5 + @vitest/coverage-v8; vitest.config.ts aliases `server-only` to test/server-only-shim.ts (no-op) and `@/*` to project root. npm scripts added: `test` (vitest run) and `test:watch` (vitest). 10 unit tests (lib/crypto/cipher.test.ts) cover: round-trip with edge cases (empty, unicode, 10k-char, JSON tokens); unique IV per encrypt; wire format (iv=12 bytes, authTag=16 bytes, ct>0); ciphertext tampering throws; auth-tag tampering throws; malformed payload throws; wrong-key decrypt throws; base64 key works alongside hex; missing key throws; wrong-length key throws. tasks.notes: Installed next-auth@5.0.0-beta.31 (Auth.js v5; supports Next 16 per peerDeps). Strategy=jwt, maxAge=60*60*24*30 (30 days). trustHost=true (single-host Render deploy; required for Auth.js to accept the proxied X-Forwarded-Host). Single Google provider with authorization params {prompt:'consent', access_type:'offline', response_type:'code'} so we always get a refresh_token (per the @auth/core/providers/google docs note: Google only returns refresh_token on first consent unless prompt=consent is forced). pages.signIn='/login' so unauthenticated redirects from auth() / requireSession() land at the page TASK-008 will create. Whitelist + user provisioning is in the signIn callback (fail closed): (1) reject if account.provider !== 'google'; (2) reject if !profile.email_verified (defends against unverified Google accounts); (3) reject if no email or no profile.sub; (4) if env.ALLOWED_EMAIL is set, require case-insensitive match — when ALLOWED_EMAIL is unset (zod-optional), allow any verified Google email so tasks.json's PRD test_step 'Войти с НЕ-whitelist-email — отказ' is testable only when ALLOWED_EMAIL is configured. (5) prisma.user.upsert keyed on the compound unique (provider, providerId) — Prisma 7 generates the relation key as `provider_providerId` (verified at runtime via smoke). Pure service layer per architectural_principles ('тонкий service layer: services вызывают Prisma напрямую, без репозиториев'). All five functions take userId as first arg and scope every where-clause by userId for IDOR protection. Design choices: (1) createChallenge does NOT explicitly set status — relies on the schema default ChallengeStatus.active and createdAt default now() (verified in schema.prisma:111,113). currentValue defaults to 0 (line 112). Avoids two sources of truth for the same default. (2) listChallenges accepts {status?, year?}. Year filter uses calendar-overlap interpretation: a challenge belongs to year Y if [startDate, endDate] intersects [Jan 1 Y, Dec 31 Y] — implemented as startDate ≤ Dec31(Y) AND endDate ≥ Jan1(Y). This matches TASK-031's archive-by-year filter (challenges that ran during a year, not just ended in it). orderBy is [status asc, createdAt desc] so 'active' challenges naturally surface above 'archived'/'completed'/'failed' in the same list. (3) updateChallenge first findFirst({id, userId}) → returns null on miss (covers IDOR + nonexistent). For owners: re-fetches existing row and validates input.endDate.getTime() >= existing.startDate.getTime() before writing. Throws Error('End date must be on or after the challenge start date') on violation — TASK-010 progress flagged that this validation has to live in the service since updateChallengeSchema can't see startDate. (4) Update payload built field-by-field with `if (input.X !== undefined)` so `null`-explicit clearing of optional fields (description/color/icon) still works correctly while undefined fields are skipped. Uses Prisma.ChallengeUpdateInput type. (5) deleteChallenge uses findFirst({id, userId}) → null-on-miss → delete({id}). Two-query pattern is fine for user-scoped ops; deleteMany({id, userId}) would only return a count, but TASK-011 spec implies returning the deleted row (typed return per acceptance criteria). Race window between findFirst and delete is irrelevant for single-user ops. (6) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client-bundle leak (cascade from prisma singleton, but explicit at the service boundary too). Exports: createChallengeAction(input), updateChallengeAction(id, input), deleteChallengeAction(id) plus an ActionResult<T> = {success:true,data:T}|{success:false,error:string} discriminated union. Each action calls requireSession() FIRST (per acceptance criterion 3 + test_step 2 'Без сессии — action бросает unauthorized') — requireSession() in lib/auth/session.ts calls auth() then redirect('/login') from next/navigation when session.user.id is missing, which throws NEXT_REDIRECT (a control-flow exception that Next handles by returning a 307). This IS the 'throws unauthorized' behavior required by test_step 2: the action does not return a success result for un-authed callers. Returning an explicit {success:false,error:'Unauthorized'} would be wrong here because the redirect is the user-facing UX (they land on /login) — same pattern as protected (app)/* pages from TASK-008. Then each mutating action runs zod safeParse via createChallengeSchema / updateChallengeSchema (delegates the schema rules from TASK-010 — title min/max, targetValue>0, endDate>=startDate, color regex, plus updateSchema strips read-only fields metric/targetValue/type/startDate/title — exercised in the smoke). On parse failure: returns {success:false, error: '<path>: <message>; ...'} via formatZodError helper that joins all issues with '; ' so a form can show them all at once. Then calls the service from lib/services/challenges.ts (TASK-011) — the service's IDOR scoping (userId in every where-clause) means cross-user ids return null and surface as {success:false, error:'Challenge not found'}. The service's endDate<startDate guard for updateChallenge throws an Error which the action catches and surfaces as {success:false, error:<message>}. STRUCTURAL CHOICE worth flagging: revalidatePath calls happen AFTER the try/catch around the mutation, NOT inside it. Reason: if revalidatePath throws (e.g., misconfigured cacheComponents in the future, or a Next internals bug), that should NOT be reported to the caller as a mutation failure — the DB write already succeeded. The current shape: mutate inside try/catch → on failure return {success:false}; on success exit the try block, run revalidateChallengeViews(), then return {success:true,data}. revalidateChallengeViews() always revalidates /challenges + /dashboard (per acceptance criterion 5 'revalidatePath("/challenges") и/или revalidatePath("/dashboard")'), and additionally /challenges/[id] for create+update so the detail page (TASK-032) sees fresh data. delete revalidates only the list views, not /challenges/[id] (the page is going to 404 anyway). VERIFICATION (per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file): wrote temporary actions/_smoke-challenges.test.ts (10 vitest cases against live Neon, deleted after run) covering all three PRD test_steps + IDOR + edge cases. Mocked @/lib/auth/session.requireSession via vi.hoisted+vi.mock so the test can flip session identity per case (owner vs. cross-user) and simulate the no-session redirect throw. Also mocked next/cache.revalidatePath because vitest has no Next.js request context — calling it bare yields 'Invariant: static generation store missing in revalidatePath /challenges'. This is a TEST-CONTEXT issue only, not a production issue (real server-action POSTs always have the request context); the mock just lets the action run end-to-end without a Next renderer. Cases (10/10 passed): (1) createChallengeAction valid input → {success:true} with userId=ownerId, status='active', currentValue=0, row in DB; (2) createChallengeAction invalid input (empty title + targetValue=0 + endDate<startDate) → {success:false, error contains 'title','targetValue','endDate'}; (3) updateChallengeAction owner editable fields (description+endDate) → row updated in DB; (4) updateChallengeAction stripped fields (targetValue=999, metric='steps') do NOT mutate the DB row — schema strips them, only description applied; (5) updateChallengeAction cross-user id → {success:false, error:'Challenge not found'}, target row unchanged in DB; (6) updateChallengeAction with endDate<startDate via service throw → {success:false, error matches /end date/i}; (7) deleteChallengeAction owner → {success:true, data.id matches}, findUnique returns null afterwards; (8) deleteChallengeAction cross-user → {success:false, error:'Challenge not found'}, target row remains in DB; (9) deleteChallengeAction with empty id → {success:false, error:'Challenge id is required'} (the inline guard, no DB touch); (10) createChallengeAction without session → requireSessionMock throws synthetic NEXT_REDIRECT error → action propagates, awaited promise rejects with /NEXT_REDIRECT/. Build gates clean: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress), npm run build (✓ Compiled successfully in 2.0s; routes registered: same 7 as TASK-008 — actions are not separate routes, they're served via the existing route handlers' POST). NOTE for TASK-013/014/015 (next pending challenges UI tasks): action signature is createChallengeAction(input: unknown) — input arrives as a plain object from react-hook-form's submit handler. With z.coerce.date() in createChallengeSchema, ISO date strings 'YYYY-MM-DD' work as-is from <input type=date>. ActionResult<T> is exported, so form code can do `if (result.success) toast.success('создано') else toast.error(result.error)`. NOTE: requireSession throws NEXT_REDIRECT in the un-authed path — the form's onSubmit must NOT swallow it; let it propagate so Next.js sends the 307 to /login. NOTE for TASK-038 (empty states / error UX): the {success:false,error:string} shape is consumer-friendly for shadcn sonner toast.error(error). Multi-issue zod errors come back as a single string joined with '; ' — fine for an inline form-level toast; if you want field-level errors, switch to returning the issue list and have the form set errors via setError per path. Doesn't block TASK-013/014/015 at the contract level.

tasks.notes: Files added: app/(app)/challenges/page.tsx (replaces TASK-009 placeholder; this was the first time the route gets a real implementation), components/features/ChallengeCard.tsx, components/features/ChallengesTabs.tsx. Page is a server component: requireSession() → listChallenges(userId) (single DB call returning sorted [status asc, createdAt desc]) → split client-side into active vs archive. The split is `c.status === 'active'` vs everything else (completed/failed/archived) — UX-aligned definition of 'archive' as 'history' rather than just the literal `archived` enum value. The dashboard already has a separate 'recentAchievements' surface (TASK-022) for completed-only, so this tab grouping doesn't double-up. Why one DB call vs two filtered ones: cheaper round-trip, simpler service contract, and the in-memory filter on a per-user list is trivial for the PRD's single-user scale. ChallengesTabs is the smallest possible 'use client' boundary — just the shadcn Tabs wrapper. Children are passed as React nodes from the server page (server-rendered ChallengeCards inside TabsContent). This is the documented Next 16 pattern: a client component can take server-component children — the boundary is on imports, not on render output. Splitting the tab interactivity into a thin client wrapper keeps the rest of the page (data fetch, card rendering, empty states) on the server with zero JS shipped. ChallengeCard is a server component (no hooks, no event handlers); whole-card click via Next.js <Link> wrapping the Card. Difficulty badges use Tailwind palette colors (green/amber/red/100/900) directly rather than CSS variables, matching the spec's 'зелёный/жёлтый/красный для difficulty'. The terracotta --primary stays for accent CTAs only. Progress bar is the existing shadcn Progress (Radix) — value clamped to [0,100] via `Math.min(100, round(currentValue/targetValue*100))` so a challenge that's overshot still caps visually. The progress comment in the spec says 'placeholder, точный progress в TASK-019' but TASK-019 is already done (currentValue is the recalc'd cached column updated on every Activity create), so the displayed bar is in fact accurate; left as-is rather than artificially gating the value. Deadline label is computed via date-fns differenceInCalendarDays(challenge.endDate, new Date()) with Russian pluralization (1 день / 2-4 дня / 5+ дней with the 11-14 special case) and status-specific overrides for non-active states (completed → 'Завершён <date>'; failed → 'Не выполнен'; archived → 'В архиве'; active+past → 'Срок истёк'; today → 'Сегодня последний день'). Russian locale via toLocaleDateString('ru-RU'). Server-clock UTC is used for 'today' since Render runs UTC and Challenge.endDate is @db.Date (UTC midnight per Prisma 7) — same convention as TASK-019/021. Per-user-tz day count is a refinement that belongs to whichever task wires user-timezone into UserSettings (PRD §5.2 hints but doesn't define a settings.timezone field; deferred). Empty state at the page level (no challenges at all) shows 'Пока нет челленджей.' + 'Поставь первую цель!' (matches spec verbatim) with a centered Sparkles icon and a primary CTA. Empty state at the tab level (e.g., active=0 but archive>0) shows 'Нет активных челленджей.' + secondary outline CTA in the active tab; archive tab shows 'Архив пока пуст.' without CTA — composing two states avoids the awkward 'create a challenge' button rendering twice when a user clears their archive but still has active challenges. Header CTA ('+ Создать челлендж') is hidden when the page-level empty state is showing (it has its own CTA) — avoids the visual duplication. Tabs have counts in the labels: 'Активные (N)' / 'Архив (N)' so users can see at a glance which tab has content without clicking. Grid: 1 col mobile / 2 cols sm:640 / 3 cols lg:1024 — same breakpoints as TASK-009's nav layout shell. Per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. VERIFICATION (all clean): npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run lint (exit 0), npm run format:check (All matched files use Prettier code style!), npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress), npm run build (✓ Compiled successfully in 2.0s with shell-overridden env vars; routes: ƒ /challenges still dynamic because of requireSession; full route list: ○ / + ○ /_not-found + ƒ /api/auth/[...nextauth] + ƒ /api/cron/check-deadlines + ƒ /challenges + ƒ /dashboard + ƒ /login + ƒ /profile + ○ /ui-test + ƒ /water + ƒ /weight). LIVE DEV SMOKE: started npm run dev on port 3939 with placeholder env vars (bypassing the .env.local NEXTAUTH_URL trailing-quote typo), curl'd GET /challenges with no session cookie → 307 with Location: http://localhost:3939/login. The 307 proves: (a) the page module loaded and executed through requireSession() without runtime errors (a render-time error would have surfaced as a 500), (b) the new component imports resolve correctly (ChallengeCard, ChallengesTabs, listChallenges), (c) the auth gate cascade from (app)/layout.tsx still works for the new content. HARNESS LIMITATION (consistent with TASK-002/007/008/009 progress): cannot verify the 3 PRD test_steps end-to-end from this harness — they require a real authed session and either a populated DB (test_steps 2/3) or the empty DB (test_step 1). Code-review proxies for each: test_step 1 (empty DB → empty state) — listChallenges([], where userId scopes everything) returns []; the page checks `all.length === 0` and renders <EmptyState/> with the spec's exact copy 'Пока нет челленджей.' + 'Поставь первую цель!'. test_step 2 (create row in Prisma Studio → reload → card displays) — listChallenges runs on every request because the page is dynamic (verified in build output: ƒ /challenges); no cache layer to invalidate, so a Studio insert + browser reload hits a fresh DB call. test_step 3 (toggle tabs → filter works) — Radix Tabs Root holds the active value in client state, TabsContent is conditionally visible via data-[state=active]; both lists render to DOM at SSR time, switching tabs is a pure client-side data-attribute flip. The active/archive lists are split server-side via the .filter on `c.status === 'active'`, so the per-tab content is correct without any client logic. Visual fidelity (warm-gray cards, terracotta CTAs, badge color mapping, progress bar fill, hover shadow, focus ring) needs hand-eyeball — the user must run npm run dev and visit /challenges with seeded data. NOTES FOR NEXT ITERATIONS: (1) TASK-014 (challenges/new form) and TASK-015 (challenges/[id]/edit) inherit the auth gate from (app)/layout. The card's whole-card <Link href={`/challenges/${id}`}> already points to the detail route TASK-032 will land. (2) When TASK-038 (empty states) generalizes the EmptyState pattern, this page has two inline empty-state shapes (page-level + tab-level) that should be consolidated into the shared EmptyState component. The inline shapes here are deliberately minimal — TASK-038 will pull them into a single source. (3) The deadline label computation (pluralizeDays + formatRussianDate + days-from-today) is a candidate for extraction into lib/utils/date-tz.ts when a third callsite needs it; right now it's local to ChallengeCard. (4) ChallengesTabs takes activeCount/archiveCount as separate props rather than computing from React.Children — explicit and serializable, matching the RSC contract for client-component-with-server-children. (5) The header CTA is conditionally hidden when all=0 to avoid duplicating the empty-state CTA. When TASK-014 lands and the user can have a 'create' button always visible (e.g., from the app shell), this conditional may become unnecessary; revisit there. (6) `archived` status is currently grouped with completed/failed in the archive tab. If a future archive UX wants a sub-grouping (Завершённые / Проваленные / В архиве), TASK-031 (Profile archive with year+difficulty filters) is the right place — keep this list page as a single archive bucket.

tasks.notes: ChallengeForm.tsx scaffold from a prior partial iteration was already in working tree but failed typecheck due to zodResolver v5 generic mismatch (Resolver<input, context, output> with z.coerce.date() makes input ≠ output, breaking the default useForm<FormValues> typing). Fixed with a single `as unknown as Resolver<FormValues>` cast on the resolver — runtime unchanged, types align. Removed the unused DEFAULT_UNIT_BY_METRIC constant (was a leftover). Added a useEffect that re-triggers endDate validation whenever startDate changes if endDate has been touched, so the cross-field refine error surfaces immediately when a user edits startDate after touching endDate. Created app/(app)/challenges/new/page.tsx — a thin server component with header (back-link to /challenges, h1 'Новый челлендж', subtitle) that renders <ChallengeForm/>. Auth gate inherited from (app)/layout.tsx (TASK-008 cascade), no requireSession() needed at the page level. Form behavior: react-hook-form + zodResolver(createChallengeSchema), mode='onTouched'. All required fields per spec: title, description, type (button-style radio), metric (select), targetValue (number input), unit (auto-fill via watch+setValue, but unitTouched flag stops auto-fill once user manually edits), difficulty (color-swatch button radio), startDate (default today), endDate (default today+30), color picker (8 swatches incl. clear), icon picker (9 lucide-react presets incl. clear). Live preview card in right column on lg+ (sticky), single-column on mobile. Submit calls createChallengeAction(payload) — on success: toast 'Челлендж создан' + router.push('/challenges/{id}') + router.refresh(); on failure: toast.error(error). Per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. VERIFICATION (all clean): npm run typecheck (exit 0); npm run lint (0 errors; 1 warning is React Compiler false-positive on react-hook-form's .watch() API — known react-compiler/react-hook-form interaction); npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress); npm run format:check (clean after one prettier --write pass on ChallengeForm.tsx for class ordering); npm run build (✓ Compiled successfully in 1728ms with shell-overridden env vars; route ƒ /challenges/new joins the existing route map). HARNESS LIMITATION: cannot verify the 4 PRD test_steps end-to-end visually (require a real authed session + browser interaction). Code-review proxies: test_step 1 (valid form → create → redirect) — onSubmit awaits createChallengeAction, on success uses router.push to /challenges/{id} (TASK-032 detail page; until that lands, the route 404s but the redirect itself succeeds — same fallback pattern as TASK-009's settings link); test_step 2 (empty title → validation blocks submit) — createChallengeSchema.title is .min(1, 'Title is required'); zodResolver routes the error to FormMessage under the title field; mode='onTouched' delays the error until first blur, but submit always re-validates and blocks via handleSubmit; test_step 3 (metric=distance_km → unit='км') — METRIC_OPTIONS maps distance_km → defaultUnit='км'; the watchedMetric useEffect calls form.setValue('unit', 'км') unless unitTouched; test_step 4 (endDate<startDate → error) — schema's .refine((d) => d.endDate >= d.startDate, {path:['endDate']}) sets the error on endDate, FormMessage renders it. NOTES FOR NEXT ITERATIONS: (1) TASK-015 (challenges/[id]/edit) can reuse most of ChallengeForm with editable=description/endDate/color/icon/status only — extract a shared ChallengeFormShell or pass an `mode: 'create'|'edit'` prop. (2) router.push('/challenges/{id}') points to a route TASK-032 will land; until then, the user lands on a 404 — acceptable per TASK-014 acceptance criterion 4 ('При успехе — редирект на /challenges/[id] или /challenges'). If TASK-032 takes longer to land, swap the redirect target to '/challenges'. (3) The React Compiler warning on form.watch() is a known incompatibility — react-hook-form's watch returns a non-memoizable function; the warning is harmless. (4) The form's date inputs hold Date objects in form state and convert string⇄Date in the date Controllers. createChallengeSchema's z.coerce.date() preserves robustness for non-form callers.

tasks.description: Zod-схемы и типы для Activity в lib/validation/activity.ts
acceptance_criteria: createActivitySchema: activityType, distanceKm (>=0, опц), durationMin (>=0, опц), steps (>=0, опц), activityDate (default today), note (опц, max 500)

tasks.notes: lib/validation/activity.ts exports createActivitySchema, updateActivitySchema, plus inferred types CreateActivityInput / UpdateActivityInput. Built on zod 4.3.6 with z.enum(ActivityType) using Prisma 7's runtime enum object directly — same pattern as TASK-010 (challenge.ts) for single-source-of-truth with the DB. Field rules: activityType required on create / optional on update; distanceKm and durationMin are z.number().nonnegative().optional() (Float? in schema.prisma); steps is z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() (Int? in schema.prisma — integer enforced at the schema layer); note z.string().trim().max(500).optional() (matches VarChar(500) in schema.prisma:134); activityDate z.coerce.date() — required+defaulted-to-new-Date() on create, optional on update. Cross-field refine on create: at least one of distanceKm/durationMin/steps must be > 0 (data.X ?? 0 > 0 across all three). tasks.notes: app/api/cron/check-deadlines/route.ts exports POST(request: Request). Single-query implementation via prisma.$executeRaw with Prisma.sql template: UPDATE challenges SET status='failed' WHERE status='active' AND end_date < CURRENT_DATE AND current_value < target_value. Returns { processed: N } where N is the row count returned by $executeRaw. Auth gate: reads env.CRON_SECRET (optional in zod schema → returns 503 if not configured); compares the full 'Bearer <secret>' header with timingSafeEqual (length-checks first to avoid timingSafeEqual throwing on mismatched lengths). Design choices worth flagging: (1) Used $executeRaw with Prisma.sql, NOT $executeRawUnsafe — Prisma.sql is parameterized, but here there are no user inputs anyway; the $executeRaw + Prisma.sql combo is the canonical Prisma 7 idiom for fixed SQL with safe interpolation. (2) Used CURRENT_DATE (Postgres) instead of computing 'today' in JS and passing it as a parameter. Reason: end_date is @db.Date (UTC midnight per Prisma 7 deserialization, same convention as Activity.activityDate per TASK-021's notes). 'end_date < CURRENT_DATE' is a calendar-day comparison in the DB's timezone (UTC for Neon). Since the schema-wide convention is UTC-midnight = calendar day, comparing against CURRENT_DATE (which Postgres evaluates as the current UTC calendar day on a UTC-configured server like Neon) is correct. A multi-tz-per-user system would need per-user evaluation, but the PRD has a single user and the current convention is uniform UTC; future per-user-tz work belongs to a separate task. (3) Used Prisma's typed updateMany alternatives considered: Prisma supports field-vs-field comparisons via prisma.challenge.fields.targetValue references but not in updateMany's where clause for Float column comparisons reliably across versions — the raw SQL is simpler, single-query, and atomic. (4) Idempotent by construction: after the first call flips matching rows to status='failed', the WHERE clause no longer matches them (status='active' filter), so subsequent calls return 0. (5) Auth comparison uses node:crypto timingSafeEqual on Buffer.from(header) vs Buffer.from('Bearer ' + secret); explicit length check first because timingSafeEqual throws on length mismatch in Node >=16. The TASK-006 cipher already imports node:crypto, so adding timingSafeEqual here doesn't add weight. (6) Returned 503 when env.CRON_SECRET is unset rather than 401 — this is misconfiguration, not unauthorized; UptimeRobot/cron operators can distinguish 'I forgot to set the env' from 'someone is hitting this without a token'. Design choices: (1) WaterLog.loggedAt is `DateTime @default(now())` — full timestamp, NOT @db.Date. So 'today' is computed as a tz-aware UTC interval rather than a calendar-day equality. getTodayWater(userId, tz='Europe/Moscow', now=new Date()) computes user-tz day bounds via fromZonedTime(`${todayKey}T00:00:00.000`, tz) for both ends — this handles DST correctly (a wall-clock day in user-tz can be 23/24/25 hours; fromZonedTime resolves the wall-clock-to-UTC instant per the IANA tz database). Returns ONLY days with logs (no zero-fill) — UI consumer (TASK-028 chart) is responsible for zero-filling if it wants a continuous bar chart. Empty days don't waste DB rows or wire bandwidth. days<=0 short-circuits to []. 'now' is injectable for testability. (4) getTodayWater uses prisma.waterLog.aggregate({_sum: {amountMl}}) for a server-side SUM — single round-trip, no in-memory aggregation. _sum returns null when no rows match; coalesced to 0. (5) UserSettings goal lookup runs in parallel with the aggregate via Promise.all. Falls back to DEFAULT_WATER_GOAL_ML=2000 if no settings row (defensive — UserSettings should always exist post-TASK-007 signIn callback, but better to return a sane default than crash). 2000 matches schema.prisma:88 default. (6) deleteWater follows challenges.ts's findFirst-then-delete pattern: returns null cleanly on cross-user/nonexistent. Returns null entirely if no rows. (4) listWeights(userId, days, now=new Date()) computes start = Date.UTC(now.year, now.month, now.day - days + 1) so days=7 includes [today-6, today]. days<=0 short-circuits to []. orderBy measuredAt desc matches getLatestWeight's contract (newest first; UI can reverse for chart). (5) deleteWeight uses the challenges.ts findFirst-then-delete pattern: returns null cleanly on cross-user / nonexistent. (6) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. (7) Note field accepts `note ?? null` in upsert update/create payload — z.coerce.date() infers `note: string | undefined`, but Prisma WeightLog.note is `String?` (nullable). Coercing undefined to null at the service boundary keeps Prisma's input narrow and explicit; an undefined update would leave the existing note unchanged (different semantics). Since logWeight is upsert-by-day, treating absent note as 'clear it' is the natural read of the input. (8) Helpers (toUtcMidnight) inlined per architectural_principles 'no premature abstraction' — same shape as in streaks.ts/water.ts, but tz-aware bucketing isn't needed here because measuredAt is already a calendar-day field. When TASK-022 wires the dashboard agg with tz-aware day buckets across streaks/water/weight/heatmap, that's the right time to extract a shared lib/utils/date-tz.ts (already flagged in TASK-027's next-iteration notes). Per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. Verified all 4 PRD test_steps via temporary lib/services/_smoke-weight.test.ts (6 vitest cases against live Neon, deleted after run): test_step 1+2: logWeight 75.5 today → row created (id assigned, weightKg=75.5); logWeight 76.0 same day → SAME id, weightKg=76.0, only 1 row in DB (compound unique upsert update branch). test_step 3: logWeight 75.5 today + 74.0 yesterday → getLatestWeight returns value=75.5, delta=1.5, measuredAt=today. Edge: getLatestWeight with only 1 row → delta=null (not 0, not undefined). Edge: getLatestWeight with 0 rows → null. listWeights: 3 rows (today/yesterday/8-days-ago) with days=7 returns only the 2 within window, ordered desc. test_step 4: deleteWeight cross-user returns null and the row remains in DB; owner deleteWeight returns the row and findUnique afterwards confirms removal. Build gates clean: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress).
